thread:
laura: @oncall-matt heads up — tenant 'acme' reporting p99 spike starting ~2026-03-17T07:12Z. p95 went 120ms -> 600ms, p99 ~480ms -> 2.1s. Dashboard: https://console/redwood/tenants/acme/metrics. I'm seeing GPU OOM events on gpu-32 in the pool serving them.

ops-bot: [ALERT] gpu-oom gpu-32 at 07:13:02 UTC — runtime-worker pid=12345 killed by OOM killer

mike: Can you capture a sample request_id + the model + batch settings for that tenant? Also paste recent kube logs if you have them.

laura: request_id=rid_0a1b2c. Model=redwood-7b-q4f, tenant default batch_size=8, kv_ttl=300s. kube logs snippet: 
```
2026-03-17T07:13:01Z runtime: OOM while allocating 256MB
kv_cache: tenant=acme size=89.2Gi slab_total=96Gi fragments=36.8%
```

jia: This looks like KV growth + slab fragmentation rather than a single allocation bug. Immediate mitigations (in order):
1) route acme traffic to fallback (redwood-3b or CPU fallback) to stop pressure immediately
2) reduce batch_size for acme to 2 to lower peak allocs
3) trigger a graceful slab compaction on gpu-32
Commands: 
```
# route to fallback model
redwoodctl routes set --tenant acme --model redwood-3b --reason "OOM mitigation"
# tenant runtime overrides
redwoodctl tenant update acme --batch_size 2 --kv_ttl 30
# compaction dry-run
redwoodctl node compaction --node gpu-32 --dry-run
```

tomek: +1. For medium-term fixes we should reduce ALLOC_COMPACT_THRESHOLD (e.g. 0.25 -> 0.12) and consider enabling evict-on-alloc for high-kv tenants. Avoid full pool restarts unless compaction fails — rolling compaction is lower risk.

laura: ran compaction dry-run, output:
```
compaction: candidates=7 reclaimed=2.1Gi estimated_frag_reduction=12%
```
Applying tenant overrides now.

ops-bot: Route change applied for acme to redwood-3b at 07:18:12 UTC

laura: within 5m p95 down to ~220ms, p99 ~480ms. No new OOMs on gpu-32. Continuing to monitor (watching kv size and fragments).

mike: Nice. Action items: (1) jia to schedule full compaction window for gpu-32 and gpu-33 and run with --safe-threshold; (2) tomek to draft allocator tuning RFC (parameters, rollback plan, perf impact); (3) laura to monitor ACME for 24h and report metrics; (4) I'll open a support summary ticket to ACME with mitigation details and ETA for permanent fix.

laura: thanks — will post updates here. :thumbsup: :heart:
